decisions.evidence: After the complete group expression, the word is a low nearly horizontal unit with a small angular raised return. Its internal letters are fused; there is no separately exposed tall crossed final t, but the stroke sequence does not securely settle either complete word. The surrounding verb is not used to decide the letters. Root places se first because the low compact unit has no independently exposed terminal t; est remains an unresolved alternative.

The initial co and dotted i are exposed. The flattened connection into the remaining letters does not securely separate a written hyphen from the joined letter strokes. H omits the visible co opening. The word is read as a whole in its two-baseline context.

The second word independently exposes co before the dotted i, followed by the same long flattened joining stroke. A distinct hyphen remains uncertain, so the two C spellings are retained at this occurrence as well.

legibility: The ink is generally dark and the large handwriting leaves most words and the three inline mathematical expressions separable. The upper 5 and lighter lower 12 are complete. Local difficulty comes from flattened connected minims, heavy terminal hooks and a small angular final return, especially in M0109, the two triangle adjectives and the ending after mutuelle. The raised les deux and its leader are sufficiently exposed to determine both words and their attachment before triplets. The heading strokes run below their words; the crossing of the q descender in canoniques does not cancel that word. C follows most of the visible prose, while H adds periods after ens, omits co twice, changes both de phrases, displaces the insertion and reads contenant. The witnesses’ agreement on mutuellement does not expose its compressed final letters, so that ending remains doubtful. Thirteen tight crops were inspected after the whole scan and both supplied halves; the first attempted multi-image display was truncated and was not counted as an inspection.
notes:
Manuscript p. 5 continues a preceding sentence with qui avec l’origine e (L01). The upper paragraph says that these objects with e form the fixed points of X_S; its parenthesis gives the expression Z/6Z and an unresolved est/se before réduit à e (L02–L04). It then names two fixed points under Z/3Z, distinct from e, and relates them to two triangles with the visible co-prefix (L05–L07). The parenthesis associates them with two triplets of mutually nonadjacent sides, with les deux inserted before triplets and the ending of mutuellem-raised-t/mutuellement left unresolved (L07–L08). These are statements read from the page, not mathematical results newly asserted here. The heading Décompositions cellulaires canoniques is underlined on two baselines; its final period lies beyond the underline. The following source prose describes two triangular faces, three edges and one vertex, then associates the faces with elements of (X_S)^ζ setminus {e}, adding that each face contains one (L09–L15). It repeats the triangle phrase and ends Les arêtes correspondent aux trois without a completion (L16–L17). The visible line-end hyphen in corres-/pondent is retained with its break; the underline is stopped before the heading period. These layout features do not create word-error rows. No deleted word or drawing is present. The insertion leader is represented by the established inserted-text convention at its observed attachment. H’s page note and en interligne are editorial language. No mathematical proof, calculation or theorem check was performed during this reading.

Root places se first in the unresolved M0109 pair because no independently tall or crossed terminal t is exposed in that compact low unit; sentence grammar does not resolve it.
